{"m": "gpt-4o", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
My uncle paid for my entire college education. I was so grateful—until graduation, when he announced I'd be working at his company 'to pay him back.' When I said I had other plans, he told the whole family I was ungrateful. The gift was always a leash.

CANDIDATE A:
A senior colleague mentored me for months, introducing me to his network and recommending me for opportunities. When I got a job offer from a competitor, he demanded I stay because of 'everything he'd done for me.' He told everyone I'd used him as a stepping stone.

CANDIDATE B:
My uncle offered to pay for my college education outright. Four years later, when I graduated, he said he was proud of me and hoped I'd pay it forward someday. No ledger, no conditions revealed—just the gift he'd promised.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:8"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both involve a seemingly generous offer that later reveals hidden conditions, leading to accusations of ingratitude when those conditions are not met."}
